chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul it descended to the First Man.
chapter_note: The chapter is dominated by systematic cosmological teaching about the First Man as head of the living soul’s limbs, with internal correspondential analogies (head/limbs, air/breath, tower/Pillar of Glory) and a fivefold noetic set (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration). The only clear late layer is the opening dialogue-question frame with an appeal to “scriptures.” One paragraph (¶7) is more mythic-narrative in tone but still stays cosmos→cosmos (no institutional application), so it is retained as core with mild uncertainty noted.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic/dialogue frame (“Once again… questioned the enlightener… He says to him”) plus an appeal to written authority (“it is written in the scriptures”), marking editorial compilation rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [...] limb of the living soul as I have written for you [...] of the living soul; he has [...] he did not know [... ...] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution/frame formula: “The [enli]ghtener speaks:” (and the leading quotation mark), per rule that apostle/teacher speech-attributions are late compilation frame.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological identity-language (First Man; living soul; Virgin of Light) presented as what the Man IS/does within the cosmic system, but introduced by a dialogue attribution typical of the later Kephalaia frame.

paragraphs.core_text: “After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [...] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal correspondential analogy (body→cosmic structure) with no citation, exhortation, or institutional targeting; mapping remains internal to the system.

paragraphs.core_text: “This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [...] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmos→cosmos mapping (First Man/head; sons/limbs; Pillar of Glory as cosmic body) in explanatory voice, characteristic of the substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: “[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n ...] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the structural correspondential mapping (head/body/air/Pillar; Virgin as soul) without institutional application; despite lacunae, the register is cosmological and systematic.

paragraphs.core_text: “[ ... ] t[h]ose [...]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [...] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [...] universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate marker: a numbered/clustered noetic set (mind/thought/insight/counsel/consideration) treated as hypostatized powers sent forth, then re-anchored to the living soul’s cosmic scattering—cosmos→cosmos throughout.

paragraphs.core_text: “And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [ ... he] gave him peace and a ki[ss ...] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [...] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his ...] his limbs and gathered his soul i[n ...] he built it in its place like this tower [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-narrative presentation (request for power; peace/kiss; gathering/building) but still entirely within the cosmological dramatis personae (Virgin of Light; Man; limbs/soul; tower/Pillar motif). Slight uncertainty due to heightened narrative/‘good tidings’ diction, but no NT citation formula or institutional targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: “[...] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [...] for[m ...] the voices that he sent [...] he might sink in and quench [... ...] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-description of restoration/gathering of soul via sent ‘voices’ (Summons/Answer complex implied) with no audience-address or church regulation; despite a minor pastoral-register signal, the mapping remains cosmic and functional.
